subject: Post-demo: latency vs unit-cost simulation & next steps
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Morgan Lee <morgan@cortexhealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: latency vs unit-cost simulation & next steps

Hi Morgan — thanks again for the demo time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can size a simulation that answers your economics question:

Recap:
- Use case: real-time triage chat + batch summarization for clinician notes.
- Preferred interaction: streaming for chat (low perceived latency), batch for nightly summaries.
- Current constraint: target gross unit economics in the range you mentioned on the call.

As discussed, to give you a concrete $/1M-token estimate under different SLOs we need a small simulation run with:
1) 48-hour traffic sample (or a synthetic profile) — prefer the 24–48h CSV extract of tokens by timestamp;
2) target p95 latency constraint for chat (you mentioned 300–700ms on the call, please confirm a hard SLO if you have one);
3) preferred model family / size or acceptable quantized option (we can suggest candidates).

Questions / asks from our side:
- Can you confirm an absolute budget target per 1M tokens (you suggested a range on the call — we need a single target for the initial simulation)?
- Are occasional 2–3s tail latencies acceptable during peak?

Proposed next steps:
- You share the traffic snapshot (anonymized) + desired p95 SLO — we run a 48h simulation comparing: Hosted standard tier (streaming-first), Hosted batch-optimized tier (for summarization), and Dedicated small pool (if predictable throughput matters).
- We'll return: expected $/1M tokens per workload, expected p95/p99 latencies, and recommended tier + batch settings.

I attached a short proposal stub (redwood-sim-proposal-v1.pdf) that spells out assumptions and deliverables. If you can share traffic-snapshot-202705.csv and the latency SLO we’ll kick off a simulation and aim to deliver results within 3 business days.

Thanks — Laura
Laura Bennett

From: Morgan Lee <morgan@cortexhealth.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 09:31:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: latency vs unit-cost simulation & next steps

Hi Laura — thanks, this is helpful. Quick answers below and a couple of clarifications from the product team.

Traffic / volumes:
- Expected steady-state: ~2.0M tokens/day (chat + summaries combined).
- Peak hour: ~350k tokens/hour (chat-heavy), estimated peak qps ~12–18 for chat requests (short prompts, streaming preferred).

Budget / unit target:
- We’re aiming for $900–$1,200 per 1M tokens in steady state. If the cost is north of $1,200 we’ll need to justify via quality gains. For procurement we want a baseline figure to model in the FY28 budget — $1,000 per 1M would be ideal as a target for the initial roll.

Latency SLO:
- Primary: p95 <= 400ms for interactive chat.
- Hard max: p99 <= 2.5s (above that is unacceptable for clinician-facing chat).

Tradeoffs / preferences:
- Streaming is required for chat. For nightly summarization we’re indifferent — batch is fine and we want the cheapest option consistent with quality.
- We can tolerate higher tail latencies for summaries but not for chat.

Attachments: attaching a small sample of chat latency profiles and anonymized traffic snapshot (cortex-chat-latency-sample.csv, traffic-snapshot-202705.csv).

Links: shared a short internal doc describing tokenization rules we use (will add to the Drive link later).

Thanks — Morgan
Morgan Lee
Head of Platform, Cortex Health
morgan@cortexhealth.ai

Subject: Re: Post-demo: latency vs unit-cost simulation & next steps

Thanks Morgan — this is perfect and gives us exactly what we need. Quick internal note and confirmation of plan:

Plan we’ll run:
- Simulation A (Streaming-first): model variants A1/A2 with streaming enabled, target p95 400ms. We’ll model cost assuming typical streaming overheads.
- Simulation B (Hybrid): streaming for chat, batch for summaries; evaluate batching windows of 200–800 tokens to find cost sweet spot.
- Simulation C (Dedicated reserved): small dedicated pool with aggressive quantization for nightly summarization (lower unit cost, higher up-front commit).

Deliverables:
- $/1M tokens for each simulation, p95/p99 latencies, recommended tier and batch settings, and a short risk note on quality/regression.
- Timeline: 3 business days after we receive the traffic CSV + confirm the model family (if you don’t specify we’ll use our recommended open model that hits your quality bar).

Next asks from you:
- Confirm acceptable model family/quality threshold OR let us pick.
- If possible, sign the non-disclosure we’ll send (we can accept the one you prefer).

I’m looping in Marissa to coordinate procurement and Vivek for the simulation run details.

— Laura
